akhfash:7-9.t:
He said ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: thus He created you; and some read it light. Whoever reads it heavy, ﴿عَدَّلَك﴾, is only saying "He proportioned your form" (عَدَّلَ خَلْقَكَ); and "عَدَلَكَ" means: He balanced parts of you against other parts of you and made you even and well-proportioned, and it is in the meaning of "عدّلك".
And He said ﴿خَلَقَكَ﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكَ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾; and if you wish, you say ﴿خَلَقَك﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكْ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾ with assimilation (idghām), because they are two identical letters, and of two identical letters one is assimilated into its companion. And if you wish, when both are vowelled, you make the first quiescent and vowel the second. When the first is quiescent there is no assimilation, and when the first is vowelled and the second quiescent there is no assimilation. «[Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect "when the first is quiescent there is nothing but assimilation".]»

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾: He made "the day" (mean) a time (ḥīn), as if, when He said ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾, He said "at a time when no soul has power" (في حين لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ). And some read ﴿يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾, making it an explanation of the first "day", as if He said: "it is a day when (no soul) has power" (هُوَ يوم لا تملك).
